summaryEn: The 17 December 1953 memorandum (Chief, Physics and Electronics Division; SI → Assistant Director, Scientific Intelligence) summarizes the current status of the Unidentified Flying Objects (UFOB) project. Per a 27 May 1953 memorandum, the P&E Division assumed responsibility for the OSI UFOB project, with duties limited to maintaining awareness of other agencies' activities (notably the USAF) and file maintenance. The Air Force retains interest but with apparently decreasing emphasis; the Directorate of Intelligence, HQ USAF, confines itself to cursory cognizance of ATIC's project (Bluebook No. 10073). ATIC's Aerial Phenomena Section is staffed by Capt. Charles A. Hardin, A/1C Max G. Futch, and one secretary within the Electronics Branch, Technical Analysis Division. Despite limited staff and several project officer changes, the project records appear up-to-date. ATIC no longer conducts field investigations (these are requested from USAF intelligence officers—primarily Air Defense Command and Airways and Air Communications Service—near sightings). ATIC's role is receipt and checking of reports, requesting additional field investigation when necessary, checking reports against meteorological, astronomical, aircraft, and balloon data, and recording findings/conclusions in a cross-referenced system by date, location, source, type of observation, and conclusion. The Aerial Phenomena Section also coordinates with the Public Information Office, HQ USAF, for public releases. Approximately ten percent of reported sightings in the past year have been classified as unsolved. The memorandum notes ATIC is in the process of transferring Project Bluebook to HQ, Air Defense Command; according to Lt. Col.
